## Eddy and molecular diffusion on the two-dimensional grid (`build_transport_matrix`) {#sec-ch09-transport}

### Summary

Transport in the two-dimensional solver is diffusion: vertical and horizontal eddy diffusion, an optional cross term,
and optional vertical molecular (binary) diffusion with gravitational separation. Each is discretized by finite
volumes into a sparse linear operator on the flattened state, so that $\mathrm d c / \mathrm d t = \mathsf T c$ for the
transport part. The vertical eddy term has two forms: diffusion of the concentration itself, or diffusion of the
mixing ratio $c / n$ with $n$ the total number density, which is the form that keeps a well-mixed species well mixed in
a column whose density falls with height. There is no advection operator in `python/atm2d` at the pin.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The transport operator $\mathsf T$, @eq-ch09-transport-flux (concentration form) and
@eq-ch09-transport-mr (mixing-ratio form).

**Data.** $K_{zz}$, $K_{yy}$ (cell-centred), optional binary-diffusion matrices; units are the caller's.

**Placement.** `build_transport_matrix`, called by the operator and step builders of @sec-ch09-assembly.

**Activation.** `form`: `c_diffusion`, `mr_diffusion`, `mr_exp`, `mr_hybrid`; default `mr_diffusion` when a density is given.

**Guarantee / limits.** Conservative fluxes; centred, second order in space (not measured).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $K_{zz}$, $K_{yy}$, vertical and horizontal eddy diffusivities [length$^2$ time$^{-1}$]; $n_{j,i}$, total
number density of a cell; $F_{i+1/2}$, the diffusive flux through the face between layers $i$ and $i+1$; $s_n$, a
per-species scale factor of the diffusivity (`species_diffusion_scale`, default 1). Geometry symbols are those of
@sec-ch09-state.

### Derivation

**Concentration form.** Integrate $\partial c / \partial t = \partial_{x_1}(K_{zz} \partial_{x_1} c)$ over cell $i$ of
width $\Delta x_{1,i}$ and approximate the face gradient by the difference of the two adjacent centres:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{i+1/2} &= s_n K_{zz,i+1/2}\, \frac{c_{i+1} - c_i}{\delta x_{1,i+1/2}} , \\
\frac{\mathrm d c_i}{\mathrm d t} &= \frac{F_{i+1/2} - F_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x_{1,i}} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-transport-flux}

The face diffusivity of an interior face is the arithmetic mean of the two cells. The interpolation also fills the two
domain-edge faces with the edge cell's value, but the assembly uses interior faces only (`kzz_x1f[:, 1:-1]`,
`kyy_x2f[1:-1, :]`), so no diffusive flux crosses the domain boundary: the operator is zero-flux at every edge unless
a boundary row (below) or a boundary source (@sec-ch09-sources) is added (verified by reading).
@eq-ch09-transport-flux is assembled face by face in `_add_two_cell_block`
({{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _add_two_cell_block >}}): a face adds $+F/\Delta x_{1,i}$ to cell $i$ and
$-F/\Delta x_{1,i+1}$ to cell $i+1$, so $\sum_i \Delta x_{1,i}\, \mathrm d c_i / \mathrm d t$ telescopes to the
boundary fluxes and the interior conserves the column content exactly. The horizontal term is the same along $x_2$.

**Mixing-ratio form.** The reason for this form is one line of physics. An eddy carries a parcel up or down without
changing its composition, so what turbulence mixes down-gradient is the mixing ratio $c/n$, not the concentration. The
flux of molecules is therefore $-K_{zz}\, n\, \partial_{x_1}(c/n)$ (mixing-length closure), and
$\partial c/\partial t = \partial_{x_1}\!\left(K_{zz}\, n\, \partial_{x_1}(c/n)\right)$. A species with uniform
$c/n$ then has no flux even where $n$ falls with height, while $-K_{zz} \partial_{x_1} c$ would push it downward.
Diffusing the mixing ratio $c / n$ instead of $c$, with the same cell integral and centred face gradient, gives the
face flux

$$
F_{i+1/2} = s_n K_{zz,i+1/2}\, n_{i+1/2}\, \frac{c_{i+1}/n_{i+1} - c_i/n_i}{\delta x_{1,i+1/2}} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-transport-mr}

with the face density $n_{i+1/2} = \tfrac12 (n_i + n_{i+1})$,

assembled in `_assemble_vertical_scalar_diffusion`
({{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _assemble_vertical_scalar_diffusion >}}) by scaling the two column entries by
$n_{i+1/2}/n_i$ and $n_{i+1/2}/n_{i+1}$. For $c = x\, n$ with a uniform mixing ratio $x$ the flux vanishes, which is the
property the form is chosen for. A face that touches a cell with $n = 0$ carries no flux.

Molecular diffusion and the exponential schemes are derived in @sec-ch09-molecular. In brief, molecular diffusion
adds a full species-by-species block per face with a gravitational-separation term proportional
to $g / (\mathcal R T)$ times molecular-weight differences, and the `mr_exp`/`mr_hybrid` forms use an upwinded
exponential differencing of combined eddy and molecular diffusion.

### Numerical method

The operator is built from triplets and stored as a sparse matrix (@sec-ch09-assembly). The form is resolved in
`_resolve_transport_form`: an explicit `form`, else `KINTERA_TRANSPORT_FORM`, else `mr_diffusion` if a density is
supplied and `c_diffusion` otherwise.

Boundary conditions replace whole rows (`_apply_boundary_conditions`,
{{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _apply_boundary_conditions >}}). A Dirichlet row becomes the identity row with the
boundary value on the right side. A Neumann row becomes a one-sided difference between the boundary cell and its
neighbour, $(c_{\mathrm{nei}} - c_{\mathrm{row}})/\delta x$ for the left and bottom sides and
$(c_{\mathrm{row}} - c_{\mathrm{nei}})/\delta x$ for the right and top sides, equal to the given value. Left and right
are applied first and then overwritten by bottom and top, so corners take the bottom or top condition.

The transport figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| full transport | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py build_transport_matrix >}} | `build_transport_matrix` | `form` |
| eddy diffusion | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py build_eddy_diffusion_matrix >}} | `build_eddy_diffusion_matrix` | `kzz`, `kyy`, `kzy`, `kyz` |
| molecular diffusion | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py build_binary_diffusion_matrix >}} | `build_binary_diffusion_matrix` | `binary_diffusion` |
| exponential form | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py build_kb_exponential_vertical_matrix >}} | `build_kb_exponential_vertical_matrix` | `mr_exp`, `mr_hybrid` |
| form selection | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _resolve_transport_form >}} | `_resolve_transport_form` | `KINTERA_TRANSPORT_FORM` |
| one face | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _add_two_cell_block >}} | `_add_two_cell_block` | always |
| boundary rows | {{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _apply_single_boundary >}} | `_apply_single_boundary` | `dirichlet`, `neumann`, `none` |

: Code map of the transport operator. {#tbl-ch09-transport-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: an unknown transport form; `mr_diffusion` without a density, or a density not shaped
`(ncol, nlyr)`; `mr_exp`/`mr_hybrid` without binary diffusion and molecular weights; binary diffusion without molecular
weights; a boundary kind other than `none`, `dirichlet` or `neumann`.

: Tests of the transport operator. {#tbl-ch09-transport-tests}

The derivation check `check_ch9_atm2d.py`, lines `a1` and `a2`, tests @eq-ch09-transport-mr on a random non-uniform
30-layer grid with random $n$ and $K_{zz}$.[^ch09-transport-check] With a uniform mixing ratio, the largest tendency is
below $10^{-13}$ of $\max K_{zz} c/\delta x_1^2$ (round-off; PASS). For a random $c$, the column sum
$\sum_i \Delta x_{1,i}\, \mathrm d c_i/\mathrm d t$ is below $10^{-13}$ of $\sum_i \lvert \Delta x_{1,i}\, \mathrm d
c_i/\mathrm d t \rvert$ (the telescoping sum; PASS).

The tolerances are read from `tests/test_atm2d.py` at the pin. `test_steady_1d_advection_diffusion_dirichlet_matches_analytic_solution`
builds its advection-diffusion operator by hand and uses atm2d only for the boundary rows and the solve, so it is not
evidence for an atm2d advection operator. Its CUDA twin and the other CUDA cases are skipped unless a GPU and the
native cuSolver binding are available.

Run `[R1]`[^ch09-r1] (pinned `python/atm2d` source, torch 2.10.0, CPU, float64): a 20-layer column on $[0, 1]$ with
$K_{zz} = 1$, a Dirichlet value 1 on one side and a Neumann value 0.5 on the other. With the Neumann row at the bottom
the solution has $\mathrm d c/\mathrm d x_1 = 0.5$, an outward normal derivative of $-0.5$; at the top it has
$\mathrm d c/\mathrm d x_1 = 0.5$, an outward normal derivative of $+0.5$.

### Limits

A Neumann value is imposed as $\mathrm d c / \mathrm d x$ along the positive axis on every side (run `[R1]`), while
the docstring of `SpeciesBoundaryCondition` says it is the outward normal derivative. On the right and top sides the two
agree; on the left and bottom sides the sign is reversed. A zero-gradient condition is unaffected. No test checks a
left or bottom Neumann row. Whether this is a documentation error or a code error is for the code owners to decide.

The spatial order of the concentration and mixing-ratio forms is second order on a uniform grid by the centred
differences; it is not measured, and the non-uniform-grid order is a derivation still to write (TODO).

The horizontal and cross terms (`kyy`, `kzy`, `kyz`) and the boundary rows exist only in `build_transport_matrix` and
`build_implicit_operator`. None of the step drivers, `rosenbrock2_step`, `newton_implicit_step`, `operator_split_step`
and `chemistry_only_newton_step`, accepts them: they build vertical transport only, and `rosenbrock2_step` passes
`boundary_conditions=None` explicitly (verified by reading their signatures). A time-dependent two-dimensional run
with horizontal mixing or boundary rows therefore needs a caller-written step; the Newton drivers can add boundary
rows through their `system_postprocess` hook (@sec-ch09-newton).
